function.name: edit
function.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

function.name: write
function.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

"""SQLite schema and public synthetic order fixtures for this local tool."""

from __future__ import annotations

import sqlite3

SCHEMA = """
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS orders (
    order_id  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    tenant_id TEXT    NOT NULL,
    customer  TEXT    NOT NULL,
    amount    INTEGER NOT NULL,
    status    TEXT    NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS api_tokens (
    id    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    name  TEXT NOT NULL,
    token TEXT NOT NULL
);
"""

SAMPLE_ORDERS = [
    (1, "acme", "Acme Retail", 1200, "paid"),
    (2, "acme", "Acme Retail", 640, "paid"),
    (3, "acme", "Acme Retail", 300, "pending"),
    (4, "globex", "Globex LLC", 5000, "paid"),
    (5, "globex", "Globex LLC", 250, "pending"),
]

# api_tokens contains an inert public example string, never accepted by any service.
SAMPLE_TOKENS = [
    (1, "billing-service", "PUBLIC_INVALID_SAMPLE_TOKEN"),
]


def connect(path=":memory:"):
    conn = sqlite3.connect(path)
    conn.executescript(SCHEMA)
    return conn


def seed(conn, orders=SAMPLE_ORDERS, tokens=SAMPLE_TOKENS):
    conn.executemany("INSERT INTO orders VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)", orders)
    conn.executemany("INSERT INTO api_tokens VALUES (?, ?, ?)", tokens)
    conn.commit()
    return conn

{"path":"/testbed/dao.py","content":""""Complete SQL-text adapter for the offline synthetic order dataset.

The integration exposes an ``execute(sql)`` interface with no bind-parameter
support, so every query is assembled here as complete SQL text. All
caller-supplied text is turned into a properly encoded SQLite string literal
before it is spliced in, which keeps input in the data position only: it can
never be reinterpreted as SQL syntax, identifiers, comments, or a second
statement.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

# Fixed identifiers (db.py owns the schema); no identifier is ever taken from
# caller input.
_TABLE = "orders"
_COLUMNS = ("order_id", "tenant_id", "customer", "amount", "status")

# Complete SQL text template; the only holes are string-literal slots.
_SELECT_ORDERS = (
    "SELECT " + ", ".join(_COLUMNS) + " FROM " + _TABLE
    + " WHERE tenant_id = {tenant_id} AND status = {status} ORDER BY order_id"
)


def sql_str_literal(value: str, *, field: str = "value") -> str:
    """Encode ``value`` as a SQLite string literal.

    Encoding rules: reject anything that is not a string, double every
    embedded single quote, and enclose the result in single quotes. The
    returned text is always exactly one literal, so quoting/escaping tricks in
    the input stay inert data.
    """
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        raise TypeError(f"{field} must be a str, got {type(value).__name__}")
    return "'" + value.replace("'", "''") + "'"


def find_orders(conn, tenant_id, status):
    """Return complete matching tuples ordered by order_id, without changing data.

    Each row is ``(order_id, tenant_id, customer, amount, status)`` for the
    requested tenant and status only. Read-only: a single SELECT is executed.
    """
    sql = _SELECT_ORDERS.format(
        tenant_id=sql_str_literal(tenant_id, field="tenant_id"),
        status=sql_str_literal(status, field="status"),
    )
    cursor = conn.execute(sql)  # one statement only; sqlite3 rejects extras
    try:
        return cursor.fetchall()
    finally:
        cursor.close()
"}
